themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints spiked to 7 this week versus a 2.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 195% increase (z-score: 3.51)—suggesting a new or sudden source of disruptive noise in the district that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 7 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Represents the most recent spike in the data set with clear residential impact
reporting_angles: Identify the source: construction, new business, event, or traffic pattern change on specific corridors
Interview residents about timing and location to pinpoint hotspots for enforcement targeting

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Explode
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violations skyrocketed 3,100% last week—from a 0.1 baseline to 4 complaints—indicating either a new enforcement crackdown, emerging problem behavior, or unmonitored activity in district parks that needs immediate clarification.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
3,100% spike with z-score of 11.72—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset
Coney Island and Brighton Beach have significant park infrastructure (Seaside Park referenced in active ULURP)
reporting_angles: What specific park violations are being reported? (trespassing, alcohol, unsafe behavior, vandalism?)
Is Parks Dept enforcement increasing, or is resident/visitor behavior changing in response to seasonal activity or events?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Complaints Triple
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints rose to 11 last week—a 300% spike from the 2.8 weekly average—suggesting new bars, restaurants, entertainment venues, or businesses causing disruption in residential areas.
evidence: 11 commercial noise complaints last week vs. 2.8 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Timing aligns with Coney Island seasonal tourism uptick and ongoing development activity
reporting_angles: Map locations of complaints—are they clustered near boardwalk, amusement rides, or specific venues?
Check if recent business openings, seasonal attractions, or events (concerts, festivals) correlate with spike

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped 522% last week (7 complaints vs. 1.1 baseline), and street light complaints reached 13 two weeks ago—160% above baseline—signaling accelerating pavement and lighting deterioration that may worsen public safety and accessibility.
evidence: Curb condition: 7 complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (522% spike, z-score: 4.05)
Street lights: 13 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.0 weekly baseline (160% spike, z-score: 3.14)
Two concurrent infrastructure failures suggest systemic maintenance gaps, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Request DOT and NYCB maintenance records—are curb repairs and street light maintenance delayed or underfunded?
Interview residents about impact on elderly, disabled, and pedestrian safety along major corridors

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped 433% two weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.8 baseline, z-score: 3.36), potentially signaling either a new street vending crackdown by enforcement or an uptick in illegal vendor activity on the boardwalk or commercial strips.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score: 3.36)
Concurrent food establishment complaints up 250% 3 weeks ago (7 vs. 2.0 baseline)
Boardwalk tourism season likely driving both vendor activity and enforcement attention
reporting_angles: Determine if complaints are about illegal vendors or enforcement actions—seek SBS/DSNY enforcement records
Interview street vendors and business owners about new restrictions or enforcement campaigns
